To determine the weight of the Mastiff, we follow the logical chain of weight relationships provided in the problem statement step by step.

**Step 1: Determine the weight of the Affenpinscher.**
The problem states: "The first dog was the Affenpinscher, who weighed only 10 pounds."
$$ W_{\text{Affenpinscher}} = 10 \text{ lbs} $$

**Step 2: Determine the weight of the Dachshund.**
The problem states: "Next to him sat a Dachshund, who weighed twice as much as the Affenpinscher."
$$ W_{\text{Dachshund}} = 2 \times W_{\text{Affenpinscher}} $$
$$ W_{\text{Dachshund}} = 2 \times 10 = 20 \text{ lbs} $$

**Step 3: Determine the weight of the Papillon.**
The problem states: "Next to the Dachshund sat a Papillon, who weighed one-fourth as much as the Dachshund."
$$ W_{\text{Papillon}} = \frac{1}{4} \times W_{\text{Dachshund}} $$
$$ W_{\text{Papillon}} = \frac{1}{4} \times 20 = 5 \text{ lbs} $$

**Step 4: Determine the weight of the Mastiff.**
The problem states: "And at the end of the line sat a Mastiff, who weighed 44 times the weight of the Papillon."
$$ W_{\text{Mastiff}} = 44 \times W_{\text{Papillon}} $$
$$ W_{\text{Mastiff}} = 44 \times 5 $$

Calculating the product:
$$ 44 \times 5 = 220 $$
